newsitem.title: USA: LS Capital settles GFL Ultra Fund suit.
newsitem.headline: LS Capital settles GFL Ultra Fund suit.

text.p: LS Capital Corp said Monday it agreed to pay GFL Ultra Fund $100,000 and to issue GFL 600,000 shares of common stock in care of an escrow agent as a settlement resolving a 1996 lawsuit filed by GFL.

GFL, a Netherlands Antilles investment fund, may sell the stock with the provision that no more than 24,000 shares be sold per month between July 1997 and July 1999, unless previously agreed upon by LS Capital.

Once GFL has realized net proceeds of $600,000 from the sale of LS Capital's shares or shares of any subsidiary, the company may spin off all remaining unsold shares of the company and its subsidiary operations must be returned to the company.
LS Capital said the agreement will eliminate a current liability of $540,000 and comparably increase stockholders' equity.
LS Capital said it has made the first payment of $25,000, and will make a second payment by September 30.
It will deliver the final payment of $50,000 by the end of the calendar year.
The settlement pertains to GFL's June 1994 purchase of $2.2 million of convertible preferred stock in Lone Star Casino Corp, the predecessor to LS Capital.
GFL converted and sold $1.66 million of its preferred stock over 16 months, beginning in September 1994.
Lone Star Casino halted GFL's conversion requests in December 1995. GFL consequently filed suit against the company.
